title: Turbine regression notebook
subtitle: A Databricks-inspired Python workspace
description: Train a deliberately simple regression on synthetic data with a chronological holdout. Python runs in an opt-in trusted local worker. No Databricks cluster, MLlib or MLflow server is claimed.

steps.title: Create the feature table
steps.concept: Keep train/test separation visible before fitting.

steps.title: Fit and evaluate a small regression
steps.code:
rows = query("SELECT wind_speed, actual_power, sample_id FROM features.turbine ORDER BY sample_id")
train = [r for r in rows if r["sample_id"] <= 12]
test = [r for r in rows if r["sample_id"] > 12]
mean_x = sum(r["wind_speed"] for r in train) / len(train)
mean_y = sum(r["actual_power"] for r in train) / len(train)
slope = sum((r["wind_speed"] - mean_x) * (r["actual_power"] - mean_y) for r in train) / sum((r["wind_speed"] - mean_x) ** 2 for r in train)
intercept = mean_y - slope * mean_x
mse = sum((r["actual_power"] - (intercept + slope * r["wind_speed"])) ** 2 for r in test) / len(test)
result = [{"train_rows": len(train), "test_rows": len(test), "holdout_mse": round(mse, 6), "slope": round(slope, 6)}]
display(result)

rows = query("SELECT wind_speed, actual_power, sample_id FROM features.turbine ORDER BY sample_id")
train = [r for r in rows if r["sample_id"] <= 12]
test = [r for r in rows if r["sample_id"] > 12]
mean_x = sum(r["wind_speed"] for r in train) / len(train)
mean_y = sum(r["actual_power"] for r in train) / len(train)
slope = sum((r["wind_speed"] - mean_x) * (r["actual_power"] - mean_y) for r in train) / sum((r["wind_speed"] - mean_x) ** 2 for r in train)
intercept = mean_y - slope * mean_x
mse = sum((r["actual_power"] - (intercept + slope * r["wind_speed"])) ** 2 for r in test) / len(test)
result = [{"train_rows": len(train), "test_rows": len(test), "holdout_mse": round(mse, 6), "slope": round(slope, 6)}]
display(result)
steps.concept: Only the first 12 readings fit the model. The last 6 are held out. Synthetic linear data is not a realistic performance benchmark.
